title: Local worker leaves jobs stuck in 'claimed' on crash; /admin/jobs list misses newest jobs
description:
Discovered testing 'auritus worker --once' against the real production API
while integrating Auritus into Pilobol.us (2026-09-14/15).

1) Worker crash leaves the job permanently stuck in 'claimed', never
   released or marked failed.

   The local worker (cli/src/auritus/worker/daemon.py) claims a job, then
   runs TTS generation. If generation raises (e.g. a missing optional
   dependency -- see below), the process crashes with an unhandled
   traceback and exits. Nothing in that path calls PUT /jobs/{hash}/failed
   or otherwise releases the claim. The job is left in status=claimed
   forever: GET /jobs/claimable correctly excludes it (it's not pending),
   so no worker -- local or the AWS Batch fallback -- will ever pick it up
   again. This happened to me three times in a row (missing misaki, then
   num2words/phonemizer-fork, then spacy, then espeakng-loader -- Kokoro's
   dependency chain is not fully captured by 'kokoro==0.9.4' alone on
   Apple Silicon, which routes through mlx_audio's kokoro pipeline instead
   of the plain PyPI kokoro package the worker-image Dockerfile installs
   for Linux/GPU) each orphaning a different job. I had to manually PUT
   .../failed with an operator Cognito bearer token (job_token alone in the
   body was rejected with {"message":"operator_auth_required"} -- also
   worth documenting, since it's not obvious from the route surface which
   auth mode /failed expects from a worker vs. an operator).

   Fix: wrap the generation call in worker/daemon.py in a try/except that
   calls the failed endpoint (with the job_token the claim already holds)
   before letting the process exit, on ANY exception -- not just TTS
   backend errors.

2) GET /admin/jobs appears to be an unsorted/size-limited scan, not a
   query by recency -- it silently omits the newest jobs in the system.

   After creating a job (confirmed via its own GET /jobs/{hash} lookup,
   which is authoritative and correctly showed status=pending), it did not
   appear anywhere in GET /admin/jobs's returned list of 25 jobs, even
   though every job that list DID return was strictly older by
   created_at than the missing one. This is what the user saw as 'nothing
   in the console at localhost:3001/jobs' for their own newly-created job.
   Looks like a DynamoDB Scan without a GSI on created_at, returning
   whatever page the scan happens to hit rather than truly-most-recent-N.

   Fix: query/scan with an index on created_at (or a sort key that
   supports it) and return true most-recent-first, or at minimum increase
   the scanned page size enough that a newly created job is guaranteed to
   appear.

Filed alongside auritus-0ae6d0 (data-auritus-api default) from the same
integration session.
